35	## Epic : Arrêt sûr de processus
36	
37	Rendre l'arrêt d'un processus depuis DevDesk sûr (bon processus, pas DevDesk, pas un processus critique) et, quand le système le permet, doux d'abord.
38	
39	Ordre de livraison : S-01a et S-02a ensemble, puis S-01b, puis S-02b. S-03 (spike) et S-04 seulement sur décision de l'utilisateur.
40	
41	### S-01a — Ne jamais arrêter DevDesk ni un processus critique, et arrêter la ligne confirmée
42	Epic : Arrêt sûr de processus — Priorité : Must — Effort : S
43	
44	En tant que développeur qui libère un port depuis l'onglet Ports, je veux que `K` refuse de toucher DevDesk, son parent direct ou le processus d'initialisation, et qu'il arrête exactement le processus que la confirmation m'a montré, afin de ne jamais tuer par erreur ma propre session, la machine ou le processus d'une autre ligne.
45	
46	Lié au bug « la confirmation relit la ligne sélectionnée au moment du Yes » (voir « Bug lié ») : cette story le corrige.
47	
48	**Critères d'acceptation**
49	1. Étant donné une ligne dont le PID est celui de DevDesk lui-même (cas réel : l'écoute d'un port-forward ou du serveur MCP), quand l'utilisateur appuie sur `K`, alors l'action est grisée avec la raison `This is DevDesk itself` (Rule 130) et aucune confirmation ne s'ouvre ; la ligne reste visible.
50	2. Étant donné une ligne dont le PID est celui du parent direct de DevDesk (seulement si ce parent est né avant DevDesk) ou le PID 1 (init sous Linux, `launchd` sous macOS), quand l'utilisateur appuie sur `K`, alors l'action est grisée avec une raison nommée : `This process started DevDesk` ou `PID 1 is the system's init process`.
51	3. Étant donné Windows et une ligne dont le PID est 0 ou 4 (System), quand l'utilisateur appuie sur `K`, alors l'action est grisée avec `Windows system process` plutôt que de laisser le système répondre « Access denied ».
52	4. Étant donné un appel direct à `ports.Kill` avec le PID de DevDesk, de son parent direct (né avant DevDesk), 1, ou 0 et 4 sous Windows (sans passer par l'interface), quand il est exécuté, alors il retourne une erreur nommant la raison et n'envoie aucun signal (garde en profondeur : l'interface n'est pas la seule protection).
53	5. Étant donné la confirmation ouverte sur la ligne `node` (PID 4242), quand le rafraîchissement du tableau change l'ordre des sockets avant que l'utilisateur réponde, alors `Yes` agit sur le PID 4242 capturé à l'ouverture et jamais sur la ligne alors sélectionnée ; le texte de la confirmation montre le nom et le PID capturés.
54	6. Étant donné la confirmation ouverte, quand l'utilisateur déplace la sélection ou que le processus disparaît du tableau rafraîchi, alors la confirmation reste sur sa cible capturée (le texte ne change pas) ; `No` ou `esc` la ferme sans signal.
55	
56	**Hors périmètre** : vérification de l'identité à chaque signal (S-01b) ; arrêt propre (S-02b) ; libellé Windows (S-02a, livré avec cette story) ; protection des autres ancêtres (terminal, `ssh`, multiplexeur) ; liste exhaustive de processus critiques (le système refuse déjà, `killFailureMessage` explique).
57	**Hypothèses** :
58	- Hypothèse: le parent direct est protégé seulement s'il est né avant DevDesk (un parent mort dont le PID a été repris par un processus plus jeune n'est pas « celui qui a lancé DevDesk »). Si l'heure de création du parent est illisible, on le protège par prudence. À valider.
59	- Hypothèse: critères 1 et 2 restent vrais sous WSL2 (identités de la VM Linux).
60	- Hypothèse: PID 0 et 4 sous Windows sont les seuls ajouts justifiés par le dépôt (PID 4 mesuré refusé dans le commentaire de `killFailureMessage`).
61	**Hypothèse retenue, non encore validée** : Q1 (seul le parent direct est refusé ; ancêtres plus hauts plus tard, avec avertissement).
62	**Questions ouvertes** : aucune bloquante.
63	
64	### S-01b — Vérifier l'identité du processus à chaque signal
65	Epic : Arrêt sûr de processus — Priorité : Must — Effort : M
66	Dépend de : S-01a (livrer S-01a d'abord ; les seams `selfPID`/`parentPID`/`procOS` et la cible capturée y sont posés).
67	
68	En tant que développeur qui libère un port, je veux que DevDesk n'envoie le signal que si le processus visé est encore celui qui était listé, afin qu'un PID réutilisé entre l'affichage et l'envoi ne fasse jamais arrêter un autre programme.
69	
70	**Critères d'acceptation**
71	1. Étant donné un rafraîchissement du tableau, quand il se termine, alors l'identité (heure de création) de chaque PID distinct qui tient un socket a été lue une seule fois et est rattachée aux lignes de ce PID (valeur brute propre à l'OS).
72	2. Étant donné une ligne listant `node` (PID 4242), quand à l'instant du signal le PID 4242 a une autre identité que celle lue au listing (processus sorti et PID repris), alors aucun signal n'est envoyé, le pied de page affiche en niveau Warn `node (PID 4242) is no longer the process that was listed — table refreshed`, et le tableau est relu.
73	3. Étant donné une ligne dont l'identité est inchangée, quand l'utilisateur confirme, alors le signal est envoyé et le comportement existant (point d'activité, message de refus du système, `PID N is no longer running`) est inchangé.
74	4. Étant donné une ligne dont l'identité n'a pas pu être lue au listing, quand l'utilisateur appuie sur `K`, alors l'action est grisée avec la raison `Cannot verify which process this is` (Rule 130), la ligne reste visible, et aucune confirmation ne s'ouvre.
75	5. Étant donné un appel direct à `ports.Kill` pour un PID dont l'identité ne peut pas être vérifiée, quand il est exécuté, alors il retourne l'erreur `Cannot verify which process PID N is — not stopped` et n'envoie aucun signal.
76	6. Étant donné Windows et l'ouverture du handle refusée (ou, en repli, la lecture refusée à l'ouverture de la confirmation), quand le signal est tenté, alors aucun signal n'est envoyé et le message dit `Refused by the system — DevDesk cannot signal PID N` (cause réelle), pas `Cannot verify`.
77	7. Étant donné la mesure du coût de lecture d'identité sous Windows (189 sockets, sans élévation), quand elle dépasse le seuil fixé dans la story (Hypothèse: à fixer par mesure avant le code ; valeur de départ proposée : 100 ms ajoutées à un rafraîchissement), alors l'identité est lue à l'ouverture de la confirmation au lieu du listing, et le critère 2 reste vrai ; la mesure et le seuil retenu sont notés dans `docs/measurements/` et `docs/architecture/network.md`.
78	
79	**Contrainte de conception (architect, décisions D-A à D-C)** : le handle est ouvert d'abord (pidfd Linux >= 5.4, handle Windows), puis l'identité est comparée sur la valeur brute propre à l'OS (ticks Linux, FILETIME Windows, `timeval` macOS), pas sur la valeur en millisecondes de gopsutil. Sans pidfd (macOS, Linux < 5.4), la fenêtre résiduelle de quelques microsecondes entre la vérification et le signal est acceptée et documentée dans `docs/architecture/network.md`.
80	**Hors périmètre** : processus protégés (S-01a) ; arrêt propre (S-02b) ; réutilisation de l'identité par un écran de processus (S-03).
81	**Hypothèses** :
82	- Hypothèse: à valider (D-D) : sous Windows, `Refused by the system` s'applique quand l'ouverture du handle est refusée au moment du signal, ou quand le repli de lecture à la confirmation est refusé. Pour les PID dont la lecture au listing est refusée (98 sur 189 sans élévation), `K` est grisé d'avance avec `Cannot verify which process this is` (critère 4) : la cause réelle (accès refusé) n'y est pas nommée. À trancher : nommer aussi la cause dans la raison grisée ?
83	- Hypothèse: les valeurs brutes ne se comparent qu'entre elles, jamais entre OS ; la valeur est opaque pour l'interface.
84	- Hypothèse: le seuil du critère 7 est un budget par rafraîchissement ; il ne change pas la cadence (2 s).
85	**Questions ouvertes** : D-D à valider par l'utilisateur ; seuil du critère 7.
86	
87	### S-02a — Dire la vérité sous Windows : arrêt forcé direct
88	Epic : Arrêt sûr de processus — Priorité : Must — Effort : S
89	À livrer avec S-01a.
90	
91	En tant que développeur sous Windows qui arrête un processus depuis l'onglet Ports, je veux que DevDesk dise que l'arrêt est immédiat et sans sauvegarde, afin de ne jamais croire à un arrêt propre qui n'existe pas pour ce processus.
92	
93	**Critères d'acceptation**
94	1. Étant donné la confirmation ouverte sur un processus Windows (`node.exe`, PID 4412), quand l'utilisateur la lit, alors elle dit : `Terminate node.exe (PID 4412)? Windows has no clean stop for this process: it is ended at once and cannot save anything.`
95	2. Étant donné cette confirmation, quand l'utilisateur confirme, alors le processus est arrêté en un seul geste : pas d'attente, pas de seconde confirmation.
96	3. Étant donné Windows, quand la touche, la confirmation ou le pied de page sont affichés, alors aucun libellé ne promet ni ne suggère un arrêt propre (la touche reste `K` « Kill » tant que Q6 n'est pas tranchée).
97	4. Étant donné Linux ou macOS, quand S-02b n'est pas encore livrée, alors le texte et le comportement de la confirmation sont inchangés.
98	
99	**Hors périmètre** : `WM_CLOSE` (S-04) ; arrêt propre Linux et macOS (S-02b) ; changement du libellé de la touche (Q6).
100	**Hypothèses** :
101	- Hypothèse: l'arrêt propre sous Windows n'est réalisable que par `WM_CLOSE` (processus à fenêtre) ou `CTRL_BREAK` (enfant lancé par DevDesk dans un nouveau groupe) ; ni l'un ni l'autre ne s'applique à un processus arbitraire de l'onglet Ports sans fenêtre (H5 du brief). `os.Process.Signal(Interrupt)` n'est pas implémenté sous Windows en Go.
102	**Décision** : Q4 (Windows : arrêt forcé direct, libellé honnête à la première livraison).
103	**Questions ouvertes** : aucune.
104	
105	### S-02b — Arrêt propre d'abord (Linux, macOS), puis forcer sur confirmation
106	Epic : Arrêt sûr de processus — Priorité : Must — Effort : M
107	Dépend de : S-01b (l'identité est revérifiée à chaque signal, y compris le SIGKILL de la seconde étape).
108	
109	En tant que développeur qui arrête un serveur de dev ou une base locale depuis l'onglet Ports sous Linux ou macOS, je veux qu'un arrêt propre soit tenté d'abord, puis qu'on me propose de forcer, afin de ne pas perdre de données par un arrêt brutal inutile, sans que l'interface se fige pendant l'attente.
110	
111	**Critères d'acceptation**
112	1. Étant donné la confirmation ouverte sur `nginx` (PID 812), quand l'utilisateur la lit, alors elle annonce un arrêt propre en deux temps : `Ask nginx (PID 812) to stop?` suivi de `Sends SIGTERM and waits up to 5 s. You can force it afterwards.` ; elle n'annonce plus un SIGKILL.
113	2. Étant donné un SIGTERM envoyé, quand le processus disparaît dans les 5 s (ou devient zombie, compté arrêté, Hypothèse: à valider), alors la ligne et son point d'activité s'arrêtent, le pied de page affiche en Info `nginx (812) stopped`, et aucune seconde confirmation n'est demandée.
114	3. Étant donné un processus encore vivant 5 s après le SIGTERM, quand le délai expire, alors une seconde confirmation s'ouvre : `nginx (PID 812) did not exit within 5 s. Force kill (SIGKILL)? It gets no chance to shut down cleanly.` ; refuser laisse le processus en l'état sans nouveau signal ; confirmer envoie SIGKILL ; jamais de SIGKILL sans cette confirmation.
115	4. Étant donné l'attente en cours, quand l'utilisateur appuie sur `esc`, alors l'attente s'arrête (le SIGTERM déjà envoyé n'est pas rappelé), le pied de page dit `Stopped waiting for nginx (812) — the stop request was already sent`, et un tick de sonde arrivé après `esc` est ignoré (génération périmée) ; pendant toute l'attente, le tableau continue de se rafraîchir et les touches répondent.
116	5. Étant donné la seconde étape, quand l'identité du processus a changé depuis le SIGTERM (PID repris), alors aucun SIGKILL n'est envoyé et le message de S-01b critère 2 est affiché : le garde-fou s'applique à chaque signal.
117	6. Étant donné un SIGTERM refusé (EPERM) ou un processus déjà sorti, quand le signal est tenté, alors aucune attente n'a lieu et les messages existants s'affichent (`Refused by the system — DevDesk cannot signal PID N`, `PID N is no longer running`).
118	7. Étant donné un arrêt en attente, quand l'utilisateur appuie sur `K` sur une autre ligne, alors l'action est grisée avec `Another stop is already in progress` (Hypothèse: un seul arrêt en attente à la fois, à valider) ; elle se dégrise à la fin ou à l'annulation de l'attente.
119	
120	**Contrainte de conception** : Rule 110 : `Update()` seul modifie le modèle ; l'attente est un tick (environ 250 ms) plus une sonde qui renvoient des messages portant une génération ; `esc` incrémente la génération.
121	**Hors périmètre** : Windows (S-02a, S-04) ; arrêt des enfants ; signaux au choix ; durée réglable ; avertissement sur les ancêtres.
122	**Hypothèses** :
123	- Hypothèse: à valider : 5 s fixe (Q2), sondée environ toutes les 250 ms. Pas de source ; Docker attend 10 s, Kubernetes 30 s. Choix de confort dans un TUI, à ajuster à l'usage (H4).
124	- Hypothèse: à valider : un zombie compte comme arrêté (il ne répond ni à SIGTERM ni à SIGKILL, il ne tient plus de socket ; le dire serait un confort).
125	- Hypothèse: à valider : un seul arrêt en attente à la fois (critère 7).
126	- Hypothèse: l'arrêt vise le seul PID listé, pas son groupe.
127	- Hypothèse: sous macOS, SIP peut refuser un signal même à root ; le refus du système est expliqué par le message existant.
128	**Hypothèse retenue, non encore validée** : Q2 (5 s fixe) ; Q6 (libellé `K` Kill → Stop une fois l'arrêt propre en place).
129	**Questions ouvertes** : aucune bloquante.
130	
131	### S-03 — Spike : que voit-on des processus lancés par DevDesk ?
132	Epic : Arrêt sûr de processus — Priorité : Could — Effort : S (spike borné)
133	
134	En tant que mainteneur de DevDesk, je veux savoir ce que `Children` de DevDesk montre pendant un scan natif, un scan `docker run` et un clone, afin de décider, avec des faits, s'il faut un écran des processus liés à DevDesk.
135	
136	**Question précise** : lire les `Children` (gopsutil) du processus DevDesk pendant (a) un scan natif (Trivy ou Gitleaks), (b) un scan par `docker run`, (c) un clone git ; que voit-on (PID, nom, durée de vie) et à quel coût de lecture, sous Linux et Windows (macOS si disponible) ?
137	
138	**Critères d'acceptation**
139	1. Étant donné les trois scénarios, quand le spike est mené, alors une note datée dans `docs/measurements/` donne pour chacun les processus enfants vus, leur nom et leur durée de vie, et dit explicitement si le client `docker` seul est vu (le conteneur étant celui du démon).
140	2. Étant donné la note, quand elle est rendue, alors elle propose un go ou un no-go sur S-03a à d (liste en lecture seule des descendants, arrêt sûr, lien workspace, lien port) avec la raison, et laisse la décision à l'utilisateur.
141	3. Étant donné un go de l'utilisateur, quand il est donné, alors seulement alors S-03a à d sont rédigées et créées dans Plane (aucun travail d'implémentation avant).
142	
143	**Durée fixée** : 1 jour au plus (Hypothèse: à valider).
144	**Hors périmètre** : tout code livré ; S-03a à d ; liste de tous les processus.
145	**Hypothèses** : H6 et H7 du brief (DevDesk ne conserve aucun PID aujourd'hui, `internal/jobs` ne stocke qu'un état et un `CancelFunc` ; la valeur d'un écran face à `:jobs`, Forward, la vue conteneurs et l'onglet Ports n'est pas démontrée).
146	**Si go, pistes de découpage** : S-03a lister les descendants de DevDesk en lecture seule ; S-03b y ajouter l'arrêt sûr de S-01 et S-02 ; S-03c les processus liés à un workspace (répertoire courant) ; S-03d les processus liés à un port (jointure avec l'onglet Ports). Reste ouvert, seulement en cas de go : piste A (PID notés au lancement) ou B (descendants de DevDesk) ; un orphelin fait-il partie du besoin ?
147	**Questions ouvertes** : go ou no-go après le spike (décision de l'utilisateur).
148	
149	Rappel des faits qui motivent le spike (lus dans le code, 2026-11-22) : aucun PID n'est conservé par le registre des jobs ni par un site de lancement du TUI ; les scans (`internal/scan`) sont annulables par `:jobs` (le contexte fait tuer le seul enfant direct, un `docker run` peut laisser le conteneur), le clone (`internal/git/ops.go`) ne l'est pas, les port-forwards (`internal/forward`) ne sont pas des processus (ils ont le PID de DevDesk, que S-01a interdit d'arrêter), les terminaux et IDE détachés ne sont pas suivis (`launchDetachedCmd`).
150	
151	### S-04 — Demander la fermeture d'une application à fenêtre sous Windows avant de forcer
152	Epic : Arrêt sûr de processus — Priorité : Could (voire Won't, voir ci-dessous) — Effort : M
153	Dépend de : S-02b (attente et seconde confirmation) et S-02a.
154	
155	En tant que développeur sous Windows qui arrête une application à fenêtre depuis l'onglet Ports, je veux qu'une demande de fermeture soit envoyée à ses fenêtres avant l'arrêt forcé afin que l'application puisse enregistrer ce qu'elle a ouvert.
156	
157	**Critères d'acceptation**
158	1. Étant donné un processus Windows avec au moins une fenêtre de premier niveau dans la session de l'utilisateur, quand l'utilisateur confirme, alors une demande de fermeture est envoyée à ses fenêtres (équivalent de `taskkill` sans `/f`) puis l'attente et la seconde confirmation de S-02b (5 s, `Force terminate?`) s'appliquent.
159	2. Étant donné un processus sans fenêtre (serveur en console, service), quand l'utilisateur appuie sur `K`, alors le comportement de S-02a s'applique (arrêt forcé direct, libellé honnête).
160	3. Étant donné une application qui ignore la fermeture ou affiche une boîte « enregistrer ? » sans réponse, quand 5 s passent, alors la seconde confirmation est proposée et rien n'est forcé sans elle.
161	4. Étant donné un processus d'une autre session (service, autre utilisateur), quand l'utilisateur confirme, alors on se comporte comme s'il n'avait pas de fenêtre : critère 2.
162	
163	**Hors périmètre** : `CTRL_BREAK` pour un enfant lancé par DevDesk ; arrêt des enfants.
164	**Hypothèses** : Hypothèse: `WM_CLOSE` est ignoré par une application console ou bloquée et limité à la session ; la plupart des processus qui tiennent un port n'ont pas de fenêtre (H5), donc la valeur pour le cas d'usage Ports est faible. Hypothèse: l'énumération des fenêtres d'un PID passe par `x/sys/windows`, déjà dépendance directe (Rule 303).
165	**Décision** : Q4 (repoussée, Could). Proposition du pm : la basculer en Won't si, un mois après S-02a, l'utilisateur n'a pas rencontré le cas d'une application à fenêtre arrêtée depuis Ports ; à trancher par l'utilisateur.
166	
167	---
168	
169	## Correspondance Plane
170	
171	Module : « Arrêt sûr de processus » (projet DEVDESK, créé le 2026-11-22 ; six work items, label `story`, état Backlog). Priorité Plane : Must = high, Could = low. Relations non disponibles sur cette édition : les dépendances sont écrites dans les descriptions.
172	
173	| Story | Work item | Priorité | Effort | Dépend de |
174	|---|---|---|---|---|
175	| S-01a | DEVDESK-708 | Must (high) | S | — |
176	| S-01b | DEVDESK-709 | Must (high) | M | S-01a |
177	| S-02a | DEVDESK-710 | Must (high) | S | livré avec S-01a |
178	| S-02b | DEVDESK-711 | Must (high) | M | S-01b |
179	| S-03 (spike) | DEVDESK-712 | Could (low) | S | après S-01 et S-02 |
180	| S-04 | DEVDESK-713 | Could (low) | M | S-02a, S-02b |
181	
182	## Won't / plus tard
183	
184	| Élément | Statut | Pourquoi |
185	|---|---|---|
186	| Gestionnaire de tâches complet (tous les processus, tri, recherche) | Won't (décision de l'utilisateur, 2026-11-22) | Valeur non démontrée face à htop, btop, bottom, Gestionnaire des tâches ; dérive de périmètre |
187	| CPU et mémoire par processus | Won't | Hors périmètre sans le gestionnaire complet |
188	| Arbre de processus et arrêt des enfants | Won't pour cet epic | Non-objectif décidé ; `Process.Kill` ne tue pas les enfants |
189	| Signaux au choix (SIGHUP, SIGSTOP, SIGUSR1...) | Won't | Non-objectif décidé |
190	| Élévation automatique des droits | Won't | Non-objectif décidé |
191	| Contrôle des processus de l'hôte Windows depuis WSL2 | Won't | Non-objectif provisoire du brief |
192	| Durée d'attente réglable | Plus tard | 5 s fixe retenu (Q2, non encore validé) |
193	| Protection des ancêtres plus hauts que le parent direct | Plus tard | Hypothèse retenue, non encore validée (Q1) |
194	| Détection d'un zombie pour le dire | Plus tard | Le zombie est compté arrêté (S-02b) ; le dire serait un confort |
195	| Arrêt propre Windows pour un processus sans fenêtre | Impossible en général | `CTRL_BREAK` n'atteint qu'un groupe créé par DevDesk ; ni `Interrupt` ni gopsutil `SendSignal` ne sont implémentés sous Windows |
196	
197	## Questions ouvertes (ce que seul l'utilisateur peut trancher)
198	
199	1. **D-D** : sous Windows, `Refused by the system` quand le handle est refusé (recommandation de l'architect). Valider ; et dire si la raison grisée au listing (`Cannot verify which process this is`) doit aussi nommer la cause réelle (accès refusé) quand elle est connue.
200	2. **Q1** : parent direct seulement refusé (retenu par défaut), et protéger le parent illisible par prudence (S-01a).
201	3. **Q2** : 5 s fixe, non configurable (S-02b).
202	4. **Q6** : `K` « Kill » devient « Stop » une fois S-02b livrée.
203	5. **Q8** : le jugement de l'utilisateur est la seule mesure de succès.
204	6. **S-02b** : zombie compté arrêté ; un seul arrêt en attente à la fois.
205	7. **S-03** : go ou no-go après le spike ; **S-04** : Could ou Won't.
206	8. **S-01b** : seuil de coût de lecture d'identité (à fixer par mesure).

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP; a Proxy row says whether a proxy variable applies, the checks themselves stay direct, DEVDESK-582) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the five checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. `test-race` is the only test run (`-race` covers `go test`); `mise run test` stays available alone for the fast local loop. CI runs fmt-check, vet, lint and build in the `Lint and build` job and `test-race` in the `Test` job, on every pull request, docs-only ones included (the docs-only shortcut applies to `Lint and build` only); the whole CI targets under 10 minutes, so run this locally before a PR to catch a red check early

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511, DEVDESK-580).** Three campaigns
in `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/` (`catalog`, `cachedonly`, `access`) replay through
`fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, cluster or secret. A `record: pending` file is never
versioned (`TestNoPendingFixtureIsVersioned`); `DEVDESK_FIXTURE_RECORDING=1` only in a local recording session.
`nexus-bench record` without `--state` applies no state filter and can overwrite an `upstream-cut` fixture.
Bench writes go only through `nexus-bench:*` tasks and the guarded `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_SCENARIOS=1` test.
Dated measures live in `docs/measurements/`; a measure contradicting a criterion or the code is frozen and noted, never fixed in the same PR.

**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
change an exact argv. The `TestMain` of `internal/app`
also replaces `detectTools` (`internal/app/scan_tools.go`, production value `scan.Detect`) with an
empty report, so `App.Init` never runs the `trivy`, `gitleaks` and `plumber` of the machine
(DEVDESK-645); `TestInitDoesNotRunTheScannersOfTheHost` and `TestDetectToolsIsScanDetectInProduction`
guard it.

**Tests and the host secret store (DEVDESK-610).** By default `credentials.Select` and
`KeyringAvailable` reach the real keyring of the machine (Secret Service over D-Bus on
Linux); a locked keyring blocks the whole suite until the timeout. A test binary that can
reach them isolates the store: `fakekeyring.Install()` in `TestMain`, then
`fakekeyring.Fresh(t)` (or `FreshUnreachable(t, err)` for a locked keyring) per test, from
`internal/testutil/fakekeyring`. `isolateHome(t)` already calls `Fresh` in `internal/app` and
`internal/ui/setup`. Two guards enforce it: at run time, any keyring or `git credential` call
in a test binary without the fake panics with `DEVDESK-610` and the operation; statically,
`TestHostStoreGuard*` (`internal/credentials/hoststore_guard_test.go`) fails on K1 (go-keyring
imported outside `internal/credentials`), K2 (`SwapHostStoreForTest` in non-test code) and K3
(`fakekeyring` imported by non-test code). The seam is `credentials.HostStore` and
`SwapHostStoreForTest`, reserved for tests (it panics outside a test binary). Limits: the
runtime guard only sees the paths a test runs; the static one misses an aliased package
name, a dynamic import and an external binary; `gitHelperUsable` reads the git config
unguarded; `Install` and `Fresh` are global, so no `t.Parallel`. See
`docs/architecture/configuration.md`, "Testing code that reaches the secret store".

**Tests and real signals (DEVDESK-708).** A test must never signal a real process. In
`internal/ports` the only place that does is `realOS.kill` (`internal/ports/procos.go`),
reached through the `procOS` seam; `selfPID`, `parentPID` and `goos` are seams too. A test
substitutes them (`useFakeOS(t, self, parent, goos)` in `seams_test.go`), and in
`internal/ui/netdiag` it replaces `processOps` on the model, so `ports.Kill` is never reached.
Two guards enforce it: at run time, a real signal in a test binary panics with `DEVDESK-708`
unless the test called `allowRealSignals(t)`, which only a test that kills a child it
started itself may do (`TestKillEndsARealChildProcess`); statically, `TestOnlyRealOSSendsASignal`
fails on a signalling call (`os.FindProcess`, `syscall.Kill`, `unix.Kill`,
`windows.TerminateProcess`, `.Kill(` or `.Signal(`) outside `(realOS) kill`. Limits: the static
guard misses an aliased import, another package and an external binary; the seams are global, so
no `t.Parallel`. See `docs/architecture/network.md`, "Seams and the signal guard".

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `golang.org/x/sys` - direct (Rule 303): the socket calls of `internal/nettrace` (`IP_TTL`, `IP_RECVERR`, `recvmsg` on the error queue); `x/sys/windows` serves `iphlpapi` (the Windows path trace, `IcmpSendEcho2`)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135, 140 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment, invalid field |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (loading or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# What DevDesk's own child processes look like: native scan, container scan, clone (DEVDESK-712, S-03 spike)

Measurement note of 2026-11-23. Spike S-03 of the `safe-process-stop` epic (`docs/product/safe-process-stop/`).
It produces no production code and no test: only this note. The harnesses that took the numbers are throwaway
programs kept outside the repository (a separate Go module in the session scratchpad); their behavior is
described below so the numbers can be redone. A dated measure is never corrected afterwards: if a later change
moves these numbers, add a new note.

Every statement below carries one of three labels:

- **Measured**: a number or an observation from a run of the harness on this machine.
- **Read in code**: from reading the repository (path and line at commit `ec457184`) or the gopsutil v4.26.7 source.
- **Unverified**: recalled, deduced or expected, and not checked here. Never to be quoted as a fact.

| | |
|---|---|
| Question | what does a "processes linked to DevDesk" screen see of what DevDesk starts, and is it worth building (H6, H7 of the brief)? |
| Machine | Linux 6.12.107 (Debian 13), 22 logical cores, 657 processes, load average about 0.7 at the start, go1.27.4, git 2.47.3, gitleaks 8.30.1, trivy 0.76.2, gopsutil v4.26.7 (the version of `go.mod`). Not a dedicated machine |
| Harness | a Go program that plays DevDesk: it starts a command through `exec.CommandContext` with `Start` then `Wait` (the shape of `cliRunner.Run`), and while the command runs it polls its own process with gopsutil `Process.Children()`, recursively, recording pid, ppid, name, command line, first and last sighting |
| Docker | the `docker` CLI is installed, but the user of this session cannot reach the daemon (`permission denied ... /var/run/docker.sock`, not in the `docker` group). Nothing was run against it and the permission was not worked around. **Scenario (b) is therefore not measured.** Podman is not installed |
| Windows, macOS | no machine available: **not measured** (see their section) |
| Not touched | `~/.devdesk`, any existing container or image, any process that the harness did not start itself |

## What `Children()` is, by reading the code

Read in code, gopsutil v4.26.7:

- **Linux** (`process_linux.go:341`): `Children()` globs `/proc/[0-9]*/stat` and reads every file, keeps those whose
  ppid equals the pid, then builds a `Process` for each. It does not read `/proc/<pid>/task/*/children`. One call
  therefore costs one read per process on the machine.
- **Windows** (`process_windows.go:675`): one `CreateToolhelp32Snapshot` of all processes, filtered on
  `ParentProcessID`, then `NewProcess` per match.
- **macOS** (`process_darwin.go:249`): lists every process, reads each one's ppid, filters. On a listing error it
  returns `nil, nil`, an empty list and no error.
- It returns **direct children only**. Descendants need a recursion, which repeats the whole scan at each level.
- A process whose parent died is reparented (to PID 1 or to a subreaper), so it is no longer a child of anything of
  DevDesk's. A descendants list cannot show an orphan. Only a PID noted at launch (track A of the brief) could.

## H6: does DevDesk keep a PID or a handle?

**Read in code: no.** Outside `internal/ports` (which reads other processes' identity, DEVDESK-709) and the
`nexus-bench` development tool (`internal/nexusbench/kubectl.go:217`, which keeps its own `cmd.Process` to stop its
own `kubectl port-forward`), no file under `internal/` reads `.Process` or `.Pid` of a started command
(`grep -rn '\.Process\b\|\.Pid\b' internal` , excluding tests). Every launch site hands the command to `Run`,
`Wait` or `Start` and drops the `*exec.Cmd`. What exists is the context's `CancelFunc`: the registry
(`internal/jobs/registry.go:290`, `Cancel`) stores it per run and per item and calls it. The brief's H6 stands:
the registry holds a state and a `CancelFunc`, never a process.

## Scenario (a): native scan (trivy, gitleaks, plumber run directly)

**Launch path (read in code).** The scanner (`internal/scan/scanner.go:647`, `:670`, `:697`, `:791`) calls
`RunTrivy` (`trivy.go:121`), `RunGitleaks` (`gitleaks.go:189`) or `RunPlumber` (`plumber.go:200`), which all call
`runner.Run`. The production runner is `cliRunner.Run` (`internal/scan/run.go:100`): `exec.CommandContext(ctx, tc.Name, tc.Args...)`
at `run.go:101`, `cmd.Start()` at `run.go:139` (stderr streamed to the progress callback) or `run.go:148`, `cmd.Wait()`
in `finish` at `run.go:163`. The binary is `trivyBinary`/`gitleaksBinary` (`trivy_args.go`, the resolved path or the plain
name). Trivy runs are serialized by `trivySem` (`trivy.go`), so at most one native Trivy process at a time; Gitleaks
and plumber are not.

**Cancellation context (read in code).** The context is created in the `Cmd` that starts the scan:
`context.WithCancel(context.Background())` at `internal/ui/workspaces/commands.go:160` and
`internal/ui/security/inventory_commands.go:244`, sent on the "starting" message, stored by the registry, called by
`K` in `:jobs`. `exec.CommandContext` has no `Cmd.Cancel` override here (no `Cancel`, `WaitDelay`, `Setpgid` or
`SysProcAttr` in `internal/scan`), so cancelling sends the default `Kill` to the direct child only.

**PID or handle kept (H6): no** (`cliRunner.Run` holds `cmd` for the length of the call and returns).

**What `Children()` saw (measured).**

| Command (argv as `gitleaksArgs` and `trivySecretArgs` build it, native) | Direct child | Grandchildren | Wait returned after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gitleaks detect --source <worktree> --gitleaks-ignore-path <worktree> --report-format json --report-path /dev/stdout --no-git` | `gitleaks`, one | none | 784 ms (exit 1: findings in test fixtures; 22 polls) |
| `trivy fs --format json --scanners secret <worktree>` (scratch cache dir, `--skip-version-check`) | `trivy`, one | none | 610 ms (15 polls) |

- One process, no sub-process, for both tools. Typical lifetime on this tree: under a second for a secrets-only scan
  of about 2,000 files. A full Trivy vulnerability scan needs the vulnerability database and the network:
  **not measured**, expected to be much longer (Unverified).
- The recursive read cost 50 ms (median) per descent here (two `Children()` reads plus name and command line).

## Scenario (b): container scan (`docker run` / `podman run`)

**Launch path (read in code).** `wrapTrivy` ends in `containerRun{Flags, Image, Argv}.cmd()`
(`internal/scan/trivy_args.go:243`), as do Gitleaks (`gitleaks.go:96`), plumber (`plumber.go:111`), kubeconform
(`kubeconform.go:87`, `kubeconform_render.go:67`, `:100`) and cosign (`cosign.go:239`). `containerRun.cmd`
(`internal/scan/container_run.go:34`) builds `toolCmd{Name: engine.Current().Binary, Args: run --rm <flags> [-e NAME]... <image> <argv>}`
(`container_run.go:42`), with the proxy values in `Env`, never in argv. From there it is the same `cliRunner.Run`
(`run.go:101`, `:139`/`:148`, `:163`) and the same `CancelFunc` as scenario (a).

**PID or handle kept (H6): no**, same code.

**What a process view would see: the engine client, not the container.**

- **Read in code.** The child of DevDesk is the `docker` (or `podman`) client process. The scan command carries no
  `--name`, no `--label` and no `--cidfile` (`grep -rn '"--name"\|--cidfile' internal/scan`, no hit outside tests):
  nothing in DevDesk's argv lets anyone tie the running container to the scan that started it.
- **Unverified.** The container's processes belong to the daemon (Docker Engine) or, with local Podman, to its own
  monitor process, and are not descendants of DevDesk, so `Children()` cannot show them. Expected from the
  architecture of the engines, not observed here (no daemon access, no Podman).
- **Unverified.** On cancel the context sends `SIGKILL` to the client. The Docker CLI documentation says the client
  proxies most signals to the container but not `SIGKILL`; if that holds, the client dies and the container
  keeps running until it ends by itself. Recalled, not re-read today, not observed.
- **Not measured.** The lifetime of the client equals the lifetime of the container run, plus an image pull when the
  image is missing. Whether the client spawns a credential helper child during a pull is not known.

What I could not measure is exactly the point the story asked ("only the client is seen"): it rests on the
deduction above. Someone with daemon access can settle it in a few minutes by running the harness with
`docker run --rm <small image> sleep 3` and reading the container's main PID with `docker inspect` next to
the harness's `Children()` output.

## Scenario (c): git clone and git sync

**Launch path (read in code).**

- Clone: the explorer's pipeline (`internal/ui/forge/explorer/pipeline.go:104`) starts a context and a scheduler;
  each repository runs in a goroutine bounded by `spec.jobs` (`pipeline.go:136`), through `cloneOne` (`pipeline.go:194`)
  to `git.Clone` (`pipeline.go:203`), which is `exec.Command("git", "clone", repoURL, targetPath)` at
  `internal/git/ops.go:44` and `cmd.Run()` at `ops.go:55`. **No context reaches the process**: the pipeline's context
  stops the walk and the scheduler, and the clones already running are awaited (comment at `pipeline.go:95-100`; decision 12:
  a cut clone leaves half a repository). `jobs.KindClone.Cancellable()` is false (`internal/jobs/jobs.go:69`).
- Sync (`F` in `ws`): `git.Sync` (`internal/git/sync.go:43`) runs `git ls-remote`/fetch helpers for tags, then `git fetch
  --quiet --prune --no-prune-tags`, then the reconcile commands, all through `runContextMax` (`sync.go:306-307`:
  `exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", ...)`, `cmd.Run()` at `:317`) with `context.Background()` (`sync.go:277`). Not
  cancellable either (`KindSync` is not cancellable).
- Neither keeps a PID or a handle (H6: no).

**What `Children()` saw (measured).** The remote was a local repository (58 MB of incompressible files) reached
through `file://`, which makes git spawn its upload-pack side like a network transport would. A plain path would
take a local shortcut with no transport.

| Command | Processes seen (depth) | Lifetime | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `git clone file://<src> <dst>` | `git clone` (1); under it `sh -c git-upload-pack` (2), `git-upload-pack` (3), `git pack-objects --revs --thin --stdout` (4); and `git index-pack --stdin --fix-thin` (2). Five processes, depth 4 | all five from the first poll (1 ms) to the end; the whole clone 4.8 to 4.9 s | the same clone with no harness at all: 4.92 s and 5.02 s, so polling every 1 ms or 250 ms did not change it |
| `git clone <plain path> <dst>` | `git clone` only | 43 ms | local hard-link shortcut, no transport process |
| `git fetch --quiet --prune --no-prune-tags` (new 8 MB commit upstream) | `git fetch` (1); `sh` (2), `git-upload-pack` (3), `git pack-objects` (4) seen only at the first poll; `git unpack-objects` (2) seen from 132 to 239 ms | 364 ms in all | |
| `git ls-remote --tags origin` | nothing: the command ended (4 ms) before the first poll could see it | 4 ms | |

- With a real HTTPS or SSH remote the transport processes are different (`git-remote-https`, `ssh`, a credential
  helper), and the depth differs. **Not measured** (no network target used): Unverified.
- The processes that matter for a clone (the transport, `index-pack`) are at depth 2 to 4. A list of direct children
  alone shows one `git` row.
- Short commands (the 4 ms `ls-remote`) are invisible to polling. DevDesk's sync runs several such commands per
  repository.

**What happens to descendants when the parent is killed (measured, with a context DevDesk does not give its clones).**
The same `git clone file://` run was cancelled through the context after 1.5 s, the way `CommandContext` would:

- `Wait` returned `signal: killed` only at 3.685 s, not at 1.5 s: the surviving descendants kept the captured stderr
  pipe open, and `Wait` waits for it (`Cmd.WaitDelay` is not set in `internal/scan` or `internal/git`).
- Sampled from outside, two of the git processes had ppid 1197 (`systemd`, the user manager) at the 1.8 s sample, that
  is they had been reparented and were no longer children of the harness; none were left at the 4.1 s sample.
- So a process-level stop of the direct child alone does not stop the tree, and a descendants list drawn from
  `Children()` loses these processes the moment the parent dies.

## Side finding: a started and never waited-for process is a zombie child

**Measured** with a stand-in (`sh -c 'exit 0'` started with `cmd.Start()` and never waited for): 300 ms later
`Children()` returns it, status `[zombie]`.

**Read in code** which launch sites do that: `launchDetachedCmd` (`internal/ui/workspaces/actions.go:233-238`) and the two
IDE launchers (`actions.go:315-316`, `:328-329`) call `cmd.Start()` and drop the command; `internal/ui/viewer/update.go:445` is the same
shape (not read past the line). `internal/browser/browser.go:15-19` does reap (`go func() { _ = cmd.Wait() }()`).
A launcher that ends at once therefore stays a zombie child of DevDesk until DevDesk exits. This is not the
subject of the spike and nothing was changed. It does mean a "children of DevDesk" screen would show a defunct
row for each terminal or IDE opened from `ws`, which a user cannot stop.

## Cost of reading the children (measured, Linux)

657 processes, 22 cores, load about 0.7:

| Read | Median | p95 | Max |
|---|---|---|---|
| one `Children()` call (30 reads, idle process) | 22.3 ms | 28.0 ms | 31.1 ms |
| one-pass table (`Processes()` plus `Ppid()` per process, 30 reads) | 47.4 ms | 51.9 ms | 54.1 ms |
| recursive descent with name and command line, a quiet child (gitleaks, trivy) | about 50 ms | 63 ms | 63 ms |
| the same descent while the five-process clone ran (19 reads at 250 ms) | 153 ms | 160 ms | 160 ms |

- The cost is linear in the number of processes on the machine and repeats at every level of the descent. On this
  machine a read every 2 s (the Ports tab cadence) is affordable; on a busy workstation or on a platform where the
  per-process reads are slower, it was not measured.
- Building the whole table once is slower here than one `Children()` call; there is no cheaper way to read it through
  gopsutil.

## Windows: not measured

No Windows machine was available; nothing was run.

- **Read in code**: gopsutil's `Children()` is one Toolhelp32 snapshot filtered on the parent id, then one `NewProcess`
  per match (`process_windows.go:675`). The repository's own comment in `internal/ports/ports.go:143` reports a
  Toolhelp32 snapshot naming 294 processes in 11 ms; that is a figure from an earlier measure, not re-taken here.
- To measure: the same harness with `git clone`, `trivy` and `docker run` argv, on native Windows, elevated and not;
  the cost of one `Children()` call and of the recursive descent; whether `NewProcess` of a child needs a handle that is
  refused for some processes; the process names (`git.exe`, `git-remote-https.exe`, `docker.exe`); and what is seen
  after the parent exits.
- **Unverified**: that Windows keeps the original parent id of a process after its parent has exited (so that a
  stale parent id could match a reused PID), and that `Process.Children()` is slow or limited there. Neither is
  asserted by this note.

## macOS: not measured

No macOS machine was available. **Read in code**: `Children()` lists all processes and reads each one's ppid
(`process_darwin.go:249`), with the quirk above (an error becomes an empty list). To measure: the same harness, the
cost per call, and whether the listing is complete for processes the user cannot inspect.

## What a "processes linked to DevDesk" screen would add to what exists

| Existing surface | What it already says about DevDesk's work | What it cannot say |
|---|---|---|
| `:jobs` (`internal/jobs`) | every scan, sync, clone, pull, index run, per target, with state, detail, failure memory, and `K` to cancel (scan, pull, index; not sync, clone) | the PID, the process or container behind a target; what is left running after a cancel |
| Ports tab (`internal/ports`, `internal/ui/netdiag`) | every socket on the machine with PID and process name, `LISTEN` and `ESTABLISHED` included (`ports.go:37`), so a clone's transport process and its connection appear while it runs | whether a process was started by DevDesk |
| Forward (`internal/forward`) | the local port forwards, which are listeners inside the DevDesk process (PID of DevDesk, protected by S-01a) | nothing is a separate process, so no PID to show |
| Containers view (`docker ps -a`, `internal/docker/containers.go:335`) | the containers of the engine, including a running scanner container, with stop and remove | that a given container is a DevDesk scan: the command has no name and no label (see scenario b) |

What is really missing, by this table and the measures:

1. **A link from a running target to its process or container**, mostly for the container scan: the client's PID is
   in nobody's hands, and the container is unattributable. Neither a descendants list (it would show the client
   only) nor an arbitrary process screen fixes the container; what would is something DevDesk puts into the command
   (a label or a name), which is a different change from a new screen.
2. **Stopping what `:jobs` does not stop** (clone, sync). That is a product decision (decision 12 and D7: a cut
   clone leaves half a repository, a sync in flight is waited out), not a visibility gap. A stop button on a `git`
   row would reopen it, and a stop of the direct child alone leaves the tree running (measured above).
3. **Orphans after a cancel or a crash.** A descendants list is blind to them by construction (reparenting). Only
   a PID noted at launch (track A) could see them, and that means a registry that holds PIDs, which does not exist
   (H6).
4. Everything else the screen could list (scanners for one second, git helpers for milliseconds, zombie launchers)
   is either already in `:jobs` with more context, invisible to polling, or not stoppable by the user.

H7 (value over `:jobs`, Forward, containers, Ports) is **not demonstrated** by this spike: on Linux, for the three
scenarios, the screen would repeat `:jobs` with PIDs and process names added.

## Proposal: go or no-go on S-03a to S-03d

This is a proposal. The decision is the user's. The evidence is Linux only; Windows and macOS could change the
costs, not the argument about value.

| Story | Proposal | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| S-03a, list the descendants read-only | **No-go** | The three scenarios show one process (native scan), one client process (container scan, by deduction) and a depth-4 tree that lasts seconds (clone). `:jobs` already lists the same work with its target and state. Short commands are invisible, orphans are invisible, the cost is 20 to 150 ms per read and grows with the machine. Nothing measured shows a question the user could not answer today |
| S-03b, add the safe stop | **No-go** | There is nothing worth stopping that is not already stoppable or deliberately not stoppable: scans stop through `:jobs`; a clone is kept uncancellable on purpose; stopping the direct child leaves its descendants running (measured), and stopping a container client may leave the container (unverified, documented by Docker) |
| S-03c, link to a workspace | **No-go** | The workspace is already the `:jobs` target of every DevDesk-started run. Linking arbitrary processes to a workspace would read the working directory of every process, which is the task-manager scope the brief ruled out |
| S-03d, link to a port | **No-go** | None of the three scenarios holds a listening port, and the forwards are in-process. The Ports tab already shows the sockets of a clone's transport with their PID |

Cheaper observations that came out of the spike, offered as raw material and not as stories: scanner containers
carry no label and no name, which is the actual obstacle to attributing and stopping them; and the launchers
that `Start()` without `Wait()` leave zombie children until DevDesk exits. If a concrete need appears later
(for example a leftover container or process that the user had to hunt by hand after a cancel), the first
thing to do is record it, then revisit S-03 with that case.

## Reproducing

The harness is not versioned. Shape: `go run` a program that starts `argv` with `exec.CommandContext`,
`Start` then `Wait`, with a goroutine that every 1 to 250 ms calls `process.NewProcess(os.Getpid())` and
walks `Children()` recursively, recording pid, ppid, `Name()`, `Cmdline()`, first and last sighting, and the cost of
each walk; a second mode cancels the context after a delay. Arguments used: the argv in the tables above;
the clone source was `git init` plus forty 1.5 MB random files (58 MB `.git`), cloned through `file://`.
